title: Saying it twice
pattern: word-word: sayur-sayuran (all kinds of) · jalan-jalan, lihat-lihat (just for fun) · pelan-pelan, baik-baik (how)
explanation: Saying a word twice, written with a hyphen, changes its flavour rather than simply making it plural. Some nouns, doubled and with -an added, mean all kinds of: sayur-sayuran (all sorts of vegetables), buah-buahan (fruit of every kind). With verbs it makes the activity relaxed and aimless: jalan-jalan (go out, wander around), lihat-lihat (just look around), duduk-duduk (sit around). Describing words said twice tell you how something is done: pelan-pelan (slowly, carefully), cepat-cepat (quickly, in a hurry), baik-baik (properly, well). With -an, a doubled verb can also mean doing it to each other: children chasing each other are playing kejar-kejaran.
natural: Lihat-lihat saja is how you tell a shopkeeper you're just browsing, and Jalan-jalan saja (just out and about) is the stock answer to Mau ke mana? Pelan-pelan, ya asks someone to slow down without sounding bossy.
stiff: Doubling isn't needed for a plain plural: buku is book or books, and after a number or banyak the noun stays single (tiga buku, banyak orang). Some words only exist doubled, like kupu-kupu (butterfly), and a few change meaning: mata-mata is a spy, not eyes.

examples.indonesian: Sore ini kami mau jalan-jalan ke pantai.
examples.english: We're heading out to the beach this afternoon.

gap.why: Going out for pleasure is jalan-jalan; jalan or berjalan on its own is just walking.

examples.english: There's no rush. Take your time.

gap.why: Doubled, pelan says how to do it: slowly, no hurry. Cepat-cepat would be 'hurry up'.

examples.registerNotes: Buru-buru (in a rush) is another doubled word. Said to someone apologising for keeping you waiting, or fumbling for change.

examples.indonesian: Biasanya kami beli sayur-sayuran dan buah-buahan di pasar.
examples.english: We usually buy all kinds of vegetables and fruit at the market.

gap.why: 'All kinds of fruit' doubles the word and adds -an, just like sayur-sayuran.

examples.english: Keep your passport somewhere safe, won't you?

gap.why: After a verb, baik-baik says how: carefully, properly. Baik on its own describes something; it doesn't say how.

examples.registerNotes: Said kindly by a host or a friend. Jaga diri baik-baik, ya (look after yourself) is a warm goodbye to someone setting off.
